title: Perspectives and challenges in circularly polarized luminescence of lanthanide(III) complexes: From solution-based systems to solid-state applications
claim: Chiral Ln(III) complexes are obtained either with enantiopure chiral ligands, which can give optically pure products or diastereomer mixtures, or with polydentate/macrocyclic ligands that form helices whose metal-centered chirality is usually racemic and must be resolved.
explanation: The first route is preferred when enantiomeric purity is required. The second places the stereogenic element at the metal but is limited by the kinetic lability of Ln(III), so chromatographic or other separations are often impractical. Brightness further requires pairing the chiral element with a strongly absorbing sensitizer, or building chiral dimers, cages, aggregates, or coordination polymers.
scope: Solution and solid Ln(III) coordination compounds designed for CPL.
conditions: Hard-donor chelates; enantiomer separation is required when the product is racemic.
caveats: Chiral ligands do not automatically give a single diastereomer; quasi-racemization of conformations remains a problem unless the geometry is locked.
